raw_response:
I’m still going to plant all 5 mu to cotton. I’ve done cotton for many years, and on this little bit of land I know how to manage it better than trying something new. Cotton takes more hand work, but with only 5 mu and two people in the house, we can still handle it. Water from the well helps, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water too many times unless it turns dry. The extension people say not to overdo fertilizer, but in my experience cotton still needs a decent base dressing if I want steady bolls later. Last year, the field with a bit more bottom fertilizer held on better, so this year I’ll keep a moderate rate, not too low, not too much. Seed I’ll buy improved local hybrid seed from the county market, because saved seed is not as reliable. For pests, I won’t spray blindly. Early on I’ll mainly watch for aphids and later bollworm. If pressure is light, I save the money. Tillage will stay traditional: rotary till once before planting, make it clean, then plant in mid to late April when the soil has warmed. If prices stay ordinary, I’d rather keep costs under control and aim for a stable harvest than chase a very high yield.
